full.text:
In this telling, the world outside the story moved first. The door adapter reported a return from the appointment, and an interruption window opened—attention became available. Authorization arrived, along with a delivery receipt and a retry request for the first call, then a second attention window. The clock ticked. More authorization and another receipt arrived, this time with a reconcile report for the first call. A third attention window opened. The clock ticked again. Authorization returned, and now a receipt and reconcile report for dinner appeared. A fourth attention window. The clock ticked, attention withdrew, and two more ticks passed in silence.

These arrivals forced the story’s shape. The return from the appointment made both promises ready—dinner and the first call moved from waiting to ready. Nina used the first attention window to queue the call reminder, then committed it when authorization arrived. The simulated speaker delivered it. But a resident, having heard the reminder, asked Nina to try again—the retry request reset the call to ready. A second attention window let Nina queue it once more, commit it, and deliver it. This time, a reconcile report arrived: the resident reported the call done. Nina closed it.

Attention remained. Nina queued the dinner reminder, committed it, and the speaker delivered it. A final reconcile report closed dinner. The clock ran out. Both promises stood closed, tied to the same returned appointment. Nothing was left waiting.
